492: Built around Custodian Guard, Allarus Custodians, and a Blade Champion core, Shield Host puts elite infantry on foot into mid-board contested zones backed by Venatari and Vertus Praetors as fast flanking pressure — the Witchseekers attachment thinning screens so the T6 2+/4++ bricks can land unimpeded. The engine is sustained primary scoring through raw OC dominance: each Custodian Guard model clocks 2 OC, so even partial squads hold objectives against anything short of a dedicated clear, while the Blade Champion and Allarus deliver precision character kills via Precision crits to collapse opposing buff stacks. It punishes transport-delivered infantry lists — CSM Pactbound and similar mech builds — because its 2+/4++ wall simply doesn't shift under crit-stacking Dark Pact volleys that would erase any other T4 unit. It cracks open against concentrated AP-3+ Melta focus fire and mobile anti-armour lists that can target and delete individual Custodians before the squad's OC advantage materialises.
438: Built around Kastelan Robots with Cybernetica Datasmith support, Onager Dunecrawlers, Skorpius Disintegrators, and a Skitarii Rangers battleline in the Haloscreed Battle Clade, this list is a layered firepower castle that combines T6 Robots with Repulsor Grid 4+ invuln and Neutron Laser / Icarus Array weapon flexibility across multiple distinct heavy chassis. The engine is an Order-cycling Datasith activating Robots into Conqueror Protocol for double-shooting Heavy Phosphor Blasters while Dunecrawlers and Disintegrators clear infantry and vehicles respectively from a planted second-row position, generating primary through Rangers holding midfield while the mechanised firing line dictates engagement range. The diverse chassis spread and layered Repulsor Grid plus Feel No Pain stacking punishes single-axis damage lists — anything relying on AP-1 or AP-2 volume to clear T6-7 models runs dry before cracking the Robot bricks. Lists that match speed and bring AP-3+ Melta or concentrated Lethal Hits — particularly Knight or Mont'ka lances closing to Melta range — bypass the invuln-and-FNP stack and dismantle the castle before its shooting output compounds.
439: Built around Sicarian Ruststalkers and Infiltrators delivered in Skorpius Duneriders, with Skitarii Marshals and a Tech-Priest Manipulus buffing Hastarii Fusiliers blobs, this is the Skitarii Hunter Cohort running a mechanized combined-arms game that feels closer to CSM Rhino-rush than traditional AdMech castle. The plan is to use Dunerider-delivered Sicarians as the damage spike — Ruststalkers with Transonic Blades punching through armor via volume and Infiltrators' Neurostatic Aura suppressing enemy LD — while Hastarii Fusiliers hold objectives behind a screen of bodies and the Manipulus extends rapid-fire range to keep threat coverage honest. The Dunerider transport shell lets it punish static gunlines and slow grinds that can't contest mid-board before the Sicarians arrive, and the mixed-profile roster generates enough activation count to win primary scoring races against low-model-count lists. It cracks open against dedicated mobile anti-armor — Knights chassis and Mont'ka Battlesuits match the Duneriders' speed and carry the AP-3+ firepower to pop transports before the Sicarians disembark, leaving T4 infantry stranded in the open.
475: Built around Sword Brethren and Castellan-led Assault Intercessors delivered forward by Repulsor Executioners, this is Righteous Crusaders running a hybrid transport-gunline that leans harder on the Repulsor's twin Onslaught Gatling Cannon and Macro Plasma Incinerator than on pure melee commitment. The engine is using Scout Squad screens to protect the Repulsor's firing position while Sword Brethren and Marshal-buffed Assault Intercessors disembark to lock down mid-board objectives and punish anything that advances to contest. It punishes static infantry lists and mid-range brawlers that can't answer both the Repulsor's S7 AP-2 volume fire and the Sword Brethren's melee pressure simultaneously, forcing split-priority decisions the opponent can't win cleanly. Fast anti-armour lists — particularly Knight chassis with AP-3+ Melta closing to 12" — crack this open by popping the Repulsor before it fires, stranding the disembarked infantry in the open at below-50% win rate.
447: Built around Chosen in Chaos Rhinos with Raptors and Warp Talons as the aerial strike package, all stacked under Huron Blackheart's Masters of the Maelstrom command structure, this is Huron's Marauders running a mid-table pressure game rather than a conventional deep-strike alpha. The engine is getting Chosen out of Rhinos onto scoring positions mid-board while Raptors and Warp Talons threaten flanks and backcourt objectives, using Masters of the Maelstrom's free Stratagem economy to sustain pressure across multiple fronts simultaneously rather than spiking one big kill turn. The multi-vector threat taxes static gunlines and transport-heavy lists that can only answer one axis at a time, and the Rhino delivery keeps Chosen alive long enough to contest primaries that slower lists can't contest back. The axis confusion in the data — sitting awkwardly between gunline, horde, and mech scores without dominating any — reflects the list's genuine weakness: it lacks the raw shooting to punish heavy armor, the body count to win primary attrition, and the crit-spike of Pactbound Zealots, so any list that commits hard to one axis and executes it cleanly will out-trade this generalist shell.
461: Built around Great Unclean One, Plaguebearers, Nurglings, and Beasts of Nurgle, this is Plague Legion — a Nurgle daemon swarm that layers Disgustingly Resilient-equivalent FNP, the Poxbringer's Lethal Hits aura, and Sloppity Bilepiper's Fight on Death trigger across a mass of T5-6 bodies. The engine is objective saturation through raw wound-pool attrition: Plaguebearer blobs sticky objectives while the Great Unclean One and Beasts of Nurgle punish anything that overcommits to clear them, grinding primary scoring turn over turn. It punishes Mid-T Mixed Brawlers and Mass Volume Hordes hardest — Lethal Hits bypasses toughness math on T5-6 chassis, and the layered FNP stack means neither Ork choppas nor Cadian lasguns shift bodies fast enough to contest. Mobile Anti-Armour (Knights, Mont'ka) cracks it open via concentrated AP-3+ Melta that chews through the Great Unclean One and collapses the Lethal Hits aura before the swarm can engage.
448: Built around Vashtorr the Arkifane leading a daemon-engine battlegroup of Venomcrawlers, a Defiler, a Forgefiend, and a Warpsmith, this is a Soulforged Warpack expression that leans hard into vehicle-density rather than the more common infantry-in-transports template. The engine is Dark Pact contracts cycling across the daemon chassis — the +1 to wound on ranged turns the Forgefiend's Hades Autocannons and Defiler Battle Cannon into genuine anti-elite tools, while Vashtorr's Keeper of Secrets ability keeps the machines operational longer than they have any right to be, with Cultist Mobs screening the flanks and contesting secondaries. The dual mobileAntiArmour and heavyGunline loading means this list punishes other mid-range vehicle lists and anything relying on T7-9 chassis without layered invulns — the combined AP-2/AP-3 volume from three distinct daemon-engine profiles overwhelms single-layer armor saves across most target brackets. Its weakness is precisely what those two axes share as vulnerabilities: fast melee threats that close before the shooting resolves, particularly War Horde Ork mobs or Subterranean Assault deepstrikes that lock the daemon engines in melee where they can't shoot and the Cultist screen is too thin to absorb the counter-punch.
450: Built around Lelith Hesperax leading Wych mobs delivered in Raiders and Venoms, with Reavers screaming up flanks, Succubi directing cult units, and Incubi as the elite murder-package — this is a Spectacle of Spite-flavored Wych Cult swarm running the full skimmer-delivery toolkit. The engine is activation flooding: disgorge multiple Wych squads and Reaver units onto midfield objectives simultaneously, cycling Combat Drug and Pain Token buffs to ratchet up melee output each turn while the opponent can't clear bodies fast enough to stop primary scoring. The layered skimmer delivery (Assault weapons firing off the move, 4+ invuln on the transport chassis, volume bodies on contested markers) punishes static gunlines and transport-heavy lists that lack the activation count to contest every objective. Mobile anti-armour lists crack it open — anything with the speed to match Raiders and the AP-3+ weight to strip transports exposes the Wych payload before it can engage, and without their delivery chassis the T3 infantry inside folds to concentrated fire.
466: Built around Infractors and Flawless Blades delivered in Chaos Rhinos, led by a Lord Exultant and Daemon Prince of Slaanesh with Wings, this is the Court of the Phoenician transport-rush at its most aggressive — Noise Marines providing mid-range sonic fire support while the melee hammers disembark into scoring position. The engine is a turn-2 disembarkation spike: Infractors drop out with Devastating Wounds on their Infractor Guns before charging, the Lord Exultant stacks fight-phase buffs onto Flawless Blades, and the Winged Daemon Prince cleans up isolated targets while the list scores primary across three or four contested objectives simultaneously. At 53%+ win rate this punishes static and slow-moving lists — Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Mass Volume Horde opponents can't respond to a threat that's already inside their deployment zone on turn 2 with AP-2 melee volume and mortal-wound shooting backed by transport survivability. Fast mobile armies running matched movement speeds — Mont'ka Crisis Suits and anything with deepstrike denial screens — crack it open by stranding the transports outside optimal disembarkation range or intercepting the Daemon Prince before it isolates a target.
474: Built around Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight and multiple NDK chassis supported by Purifiers, Castellan Crowe, and Interceptors, this is the Sanctic Spearhead shape — T7 walkers with 4+ invuln and Nemesis force weapons providing Lethal Hits in melee, backed by Purifier massed-attack crit stacking and Brotherhood Librarian psychic buffs. The engine is closing distance via Interceptor teleport-shunt and GMNDK alpha-strike charges, dropping mortals through Nemesis force weapon Lethal Hits procs while Purifiers clean up with their volume-attack crit spam, all while NDKs sticky mid-board objectives. The 4+ invuln on multiple T7 chassis punishes shooting-dependent lists that can't crack durable walkers efficiently, particularly static gunlines and skimmer-fire lists whose AP-1/AP-2 volume simply bounces off Aegis saves. However, the list folds to concentrated AP-3+ Melta focus fire and mobile anti-armour lists that match NDK movement while threatening to delete a 200-point walker per activation, collapsing the scoring engine faster than Interceptor repositioning can compensate.
473: Built around Paladins and Brotherhood Terminators anchored by Grand Master Voldus and a Brotherhood Chaplain, this is the Hallowed Conclave's premium Terminator hammer — deep-striking elite infantry delivering concentrated melee violence behind a screen of Interceptors running secondary objectives. The engine is Voldus-buffed Paladins dropping into engagement range via Teleport Strike, stacking the Chaplain's Litanies to spike Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 on the charge while Interceptors use their 12" move + Teleporter Boost to claim and contest secondaries the opponent can't reach. At 51% win rate this is a competitively honest but unforgiving list — it punishes static gunlines and Mass Volume Horde infantry blobs that can't clear 2+/4++ Terminator bodies off objectives before the primary gap opens. It cracks when facing layered-AP shooting or fast anti-armour vehicle lists that pick off the Terminator delivery wave before it engages, leaving the army's limited activation count unable to recover on primary.
481: Built around Knight Castellans and Knight Destriers — the Questoris Companions long-range platform paired with Wardog screening bodies — this is a planted-then-pivot list that leans on the Castellan's Plasma Decimator and Volcano Lance to do sustained anti-armour work from mid-table while Destriers hold flanks and contest objectives. The engine scores by forcing the opponent into bad trades: the Castellan's 72" Volcano Lance threatens any T9+ chassis from deployment, while the Destrier screen eats incoming charges and buys shooting turns. Ion shields on every chassis (4+ invuln) absorb the alpha strike that would otherwise crack the Castellan before it fires twice, and the Inquisitorial Agents slot fills out secondary-scoring reach that a pure big-knight list can't match. It punishes slow durable-grind lists — Death Guard Vectorium and Mass Volume Horde blobs specifically — because AP-3+ Volcano Lance fire and Plasma Decimator Blast templates clear T5-9 chassis and infantry screens alike without needing to close range. It struggles badly into mobile melee hordes like War Horde Orks or Subterranean Assault GSC, which can tarpit Destriers turn 1 and lock the Castellan in melee before its long-range superiority pays off.
480: Built around swarms of Armiger Helverins and Warglaives supported by one or two TITANIC anchors — a Warden, Paladin, or Crusader — with a Callidus Assassin providing disruption, this is the activation-count answer to Imperial Knights' usual low-model-count problem. The plan is to flood the board with 10–12 fast T9 chassis generating constant AP-3+ autocannon and chainsword pressure across every objective, outscoring opponents on primary while the big Knights and Callidus eliminate key characters and screens. With 4+ ion-shield invulns on every Armiger and the big Knights absorbing focus fire, it punishes elite melee and anti-tank-light lists that can't efficiently crack T9 across a dozen activations. Its real vulnerability is mass-infantry hordes and Transport Infantry — War Horde's Sustained Hits 1 mob charges and Pactbound Zealots' Cultist screens plus Possessed hammers generate enough bodies and activations to contest every objective simultaneously, spreading the Armiger fire too thin to ever clear a scoring unit.
430: Built around a Hekaton Land Fortress anchoring the midfield, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn fire platforms, and Einhyr Hearthguard as the melee hammer, this is a Hearthband brick — dense T5-6 bodies backed by a T10+ transport that never truly stops being a threat even when empty. The engine is mixed-range saturation: Thunderkyn and Ironkin Steeljacks with Heavy Volkanite Disintegrators push AP-2 volume at mid-range while Hernkyn Pioneers screen forward objectives and the Hearthguard disembark to punish anything that closes, with the Memnyr Strategist cycling strats to keep the damage chain live. It punishes Mid-T Mixed Brawler rosters and infantry blobs hard — Volkanite Disintegrator Lethal Hits triggers sidestep T5-6 toughness math, and the Fortress's sheer wound pool forces opponents to commit disproportionate anti-tank firepower before the Hearthguard ever need to swing. Against fast kite lists like Drukhari Reaper's Wager or Aspect Host, the lack of meaningful mobility exposes the brick — the Fortress can't chase skimmers, and Pioneers alone can't hold contested secondaries against a list that refuses engagement.
482: Built around Cerastus Knight Atrapos and Cerastus Knight Lancer supported by Canis Rex, this is a Questor Allegiant-style mobile lance that puts fast T12 chassis with 4+ ion-shield invulns into the opponent's face rather than planting in a gunline. The engine is concentrated AP-3+ Melta and the Atrapos's Atrapos Lascutter (Lethal Hits, AP-4, D6+2 damage) closing on priority targets turn 1 via the Cerastus chassis's 14" base movement, while Canis Rex and Armiger Warglaives clean up what survives and contest secondaries. It punishes durable mid-board lists — Plague Marines, Custodian Guard, T9 vehicles — where the Atrapos's Lethal Hits cuts through layered FNP and 4+ invulns that stop conventional AP-2 fire. Slow horde lists and transport-heavy infantry spam crack it open, however: with only 6–8 activations the Knights bleed primary scoring against mobs that simply occupy more objectives than the lance can clear in a turn.
456: Built around Canoptek Wraiths anchored by a Technomancer and backed by multiple C'tan Shards — Nightbringer, Void Dragon, and the Deceiver — this is Awakened Dynasty at its most oppressive, flooding midfield with 4+ invulnerable, reanimating bodies while Scarab Swarms screen the flanks. The engine is positional stranglehold: Wraiths claim and hold mid-board objectives that opponents can't efficiently clear through 4+ invuln plus Technomancer reanimation, while each C'tan shard independently threatens a different target priority — Nightbringer punishes infantry clusters, Void Dragon cracks vehicles, the Deceiver repositions to wherever the scoring gap opens. It punishes Heavy Gunline and Transport Infantry lists hard, because static Russes and Rhino-rush Possessed both lack the activation density to clear reanimating Wraiths off objectives before the primary score compounds beyond recovery. The weakness is concentrated AP-3+ Melta pressure from Mobile Anti-Armour lists — Knight chassis or Mont'ka Battlesuits that focus-fire each C'tan in sequence drain the list's damage output before the Wraith grind can close the score gap.
486: Built around towering Boyz mobs backed by Warboss and Big Boss character stacks, Painboy FNP bubbles, and Stormboyz as fast flanking threats, this is War Horde running its purest Green Tide expression — Ghazghkull riding in a Battlewagon or joining a Boyz unit to solve his target-priority problem while Sustained Hits 1 lifts every Slugga swing across the roster. The win condition is raw OC dominance: flood three to five objectives with 20-30 Boyz blobs turn one, park Painboy within 3" to stack a feel-no-pain layer over the base toughness, and dare the opponent to clear enough models before running out of their own activations. It punishes low-activation vehicle lists and planted gunlines hardest — a 12-15 activation Ork roster overwhelms the firing-arc economy of Russ tank companies or Knight lists that can't process the wave before Ghazghkull's unit crashes into their front line. Fast skimmer lists are the natural crack: Drukhari Raiders and Wave Serpents sit at 24-30" pumping Splinter fire and Dark Lances into the mob without ever entering charge range, and without reliable melee engagement the Sustained Hits 1 damage engine never fires.
431: Built around Cthonian Berserks delivered by Sagitaurs, backed by Brôkhyr Thunderkyn fire support and an Einhyr Hearthguard anvil anchored to a Hekaton Land Fortress, this is the Leagues of Votann Hearthband brawler in its most aggressive expression. The plan is to push Sagitaurs forward turn 1, disgorge Berserks onto mid-board objectives where their T5 frames and Lethal Hits melee profile grind through whatever contests them, while Thunderkyn and the Land Fortress delete anything too tough for the Berserks to chew. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists badly — the Sagitaur delivery gives it the speed to reach Russ and Knight chassis before they can dictate the trade, and Hernkyn Pioneers steal secondary scoring that slow lists can't answer. It cracks open against fast skimmer fire and mobile anti-armour: Raider kiting bleeds Berserks before they engage, and concentrated AP-3 Melta from Knights or Mont'ka Crisis suits pops Sagitaurs on approach and strands the hammers mid-table.
487: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Kill Rig, and dual Beastboss characters — including Mozrog Skragbad — this is Da Big Hunt running at full throttle, a dedicated Beast Snagga-only roster that brings T5-6 bodies in volume backed by a T10 Monster anchor. The engine is simple: advance the Beast Snagga Boyz blob onto midfield objectives while Squighog Boyz threaten early charges on vehicles and monsters, with Kill Rig providing Lethal Hits aura support and Mozrog delivering a devastating Sustained Hits melee spike that cracks T9+ chassis opponents thought were safe. At 64.9% win rate, this list punishes low-activation vehicle lists — Knights and Mont'ka especially — by flooding objectives with high-OC bodies they can't clear before Squighogs lock them in melee where their guns go silent. It struggles badly against Drukhari Reaper's Wager and Aeldari Aspect Host kite lists, which chip the Beast Snagga blobs at 24–30" range all game, denying the charge windows that the entire damage engine depends on.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan and Adrax Agatone stacking flame buffs onto Infernus Squads and Eradicators delivered inside a Land Raider Redeemer, this is a Firestorm Assault Force expression that marries heavy-weapon fire support with melta-and-flame transport-rush. The engine is straightforward: Vulkan's re-roll wound aura plus Agatone's Strength 5 flame upgrade turns the Redeemer's twin Heavy Flamers and Infernus Squads' Pyreblasters into AP-2 volume that clears anything short of T8, while Eradicators supply the AP-4 D6 damage to crack whatever armor survived the heat. It punishes static infantry-heavy lists and slow gunlines hard — both Heavy Gunline Toolbox Russ companies and Mass Volume Horde blobs evaporate when flamers auto-hit through cover and Eradicators fire twice at half range. Fragile fast platforms that stay at 30"+ (Drukhari Raiders, Wave Serpents) and mobile melee threats that can tie up the Redeemer before it disgorges cargo are the real threats, since the entire offense collapses if the transport dies before it delivers or the flame characters get sniped via Precision.
488:
Built around Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Tankbustas, and Flash Gitz backed by Mek support characters, this is War Horde's rarely-seen long-range grot-and-gunner variant — a shooty Ork castle that floods objectives with cheap bodies while specialist ranged units do the real damage.

The plan is to plant a massive grot-and-Boyz screen across mid-table to generate OC and absorb charges while the Shokk Attack Gun, Lootas, and Flash Gitz grind through enemy units at range, with Tankbustas providing dedicated anti-armour punch against vehicles and Monsters that close in.

It punishes slow static armies and low-activation lists — Heavy Gunline opponents who expect to dictate range find themselves outbodied on objectives while Shokk Attack Gun's randomized Strength and Blast profile deletes clumped infantry surprisingly efficiently.

Its below-average win rate exposes the core tension: Drukhari and Aeldari skimmers simply fire-and-fade outside the guns' effective band, chipping the screen with volume fire that Ork 6+ armor can't handle, while the list lacks the guaranteed melee threat of War Horde's standard Sustained Hits 1 mob engine to punish opponents who refuse the engagement.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar leading Victrix Honour Guard as a near-unkillable melee anchor, backed by Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts as the long-range heavy-weapons platform, this is an Anvil Siege Force or Ironstorm Spearhead expression that pairs a durable midfield hammer with a punishing static gunline. The plan is to plant the Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus batteries in firing lanes while Calgar's Victrix brick holds midfield objectives under fire, scoring primary through a combination of high-OC anchor units and Scout/Incursor screening that denies the opponent forward positions. The Repulsor Executioners' Macro Plasma Incinerators and the Ballistus's Twin Lascannons at AP-3/AP-4 absolutely punish low-model-count elite lists — Knights, Mont'ka Battlesuits, and Chaos Daemon Engines that expose T7-9 chassis to concentrated fire will fold to the volume of high-AP shots per turn. Fast kite lists running Wave Serpents or Raiders, however, can dance outside the optimal 24-36" firing envelopes and strip the relatively immobile heavy chassis piecemeal before Calgar's brick can threaten them across the board.
478: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry, Wulfen with Storm Shields, and Wolf Guard Terminators anchored by Bjorn the Fell-Handed, this is a Champions of Russ list — or more accurately, the community's "Wolf Jail" variant — that layers a durable elite melee core behind Scout Squad screens. The plan is to use Scout mobility to deny early deepstrike lanes and hold home objectives while the Thunderwolves and Wulfen close at 10"+ threat range, forcing the opponent into melee on your terms while Bjorn's dreadnought firepower chips characters and key targets. It punishes mid-board brawler lists and transport infantry through sheer activation volume and the Wulfen's Storm Shield 4++ absorbing the counter-punch that usually breaks elite-melee armies. Its spread across six playstyle axes with no dominant one above 6.7 reveals the weakness: it has no decisive engine, and focused anti-elite shooting — Dark Reapers with Lethal Hits, or Russ Demolisher fire cracking T5 Terminators through AP-3 — outpaces its ability to close the distance before the score gap opens.
428: Built around The Twin Lance superheavy flyer alongside Riptides, Broadsides, Pathfinders, and Stealth Battlesuits in a Mont'ka-style mobile-gunline shell, this is a T'au anti-armour platform list that uses its air superiority anchor to threaten high-T targets while the ground suite handles everything else. The engine is concentrated AP-3+ and Melta-equivalent firepower delivered via Jump-Shoot-Jump Crisis positioning and Twin Lance strafing runs, with Pathfinder Markerlight stacking converting hit-rerolls into reliable wound thresholds against T9-12 chassis while Broadsides and Riptides grind secondary objectives. It punishes static Heavy Gunline lists hard — the Twin Lance and JSJ repositioning deny firing arcs entirely, and once Riptides close to heavy-burst-cannon range, Russ-equivalent chassis can't absorb the sustained AP-2 volume. Against mobile brawlers and melee tarpits it struggles badly, as War Horde Boyz mobs can close the gap and lock Riptides in melee before the gunline can reposition, collapsing the JSJ rhythm that the entire damage engine depends on.
483: Built around a Broodlord-led Genestealer swarm reinforced by Lictors, Deathleaper, Von Ryan's Leapers, and a Neurolictor, this is Assimilation Swarm at its most concentrated — a deep-striking infiltration cult that floods the board with high-movement melee threats before the opponent can establish a firing line. It wins by using Deathleaper and the Neurolictor to strip Leadership and deny Overwatch, then delivering Genestealers and Von Ryan's Leapers into isolated targets via infiltrate and reserves, while the Broodlord's melee buffs amplify the charge spike enough to clear objective holders in a single activation. The 4+ invuln on Genestealers and the sheer body count make it punishing against static gunlines and transport-delivered infantry that can't screen deep enough to keep the swarm off their hammers. It struggles into Lethal Hits walls — Plague Marines with Disgustingly Resilient and Plagueburst Crawler indirect fire, or Custodes at 2+/4++, absorb the charge volume without breaking and grind back through the relatively low wound pools once the initial wave is spent.
490: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened on Disc, Sekhetar Robots, a winged Daemon Prince of Tzeentch, and Daemon Engine fire support from Defilers and Forgefiends, this is a Cult of Magic list that weaponizes the Tzeentch invulnerable-save stack alongside Lethal Hits volume to grind opponents into the ground. The engine is the Enlightened's Disc-mounted mobility delivering Lethal Hits-proccing attacks through Psychic Ritual buffs while the Sekhetar Robots and Daemon Engines pour AP-2+ firepower into mid-board — the Daemon Prince serves as both buff node and melee threat, cycling Cabbalistic Rituals to spike damage when the trade window opens. It punishes slow durable lists like AM Grizzled Company and Death Guard Vectorium that can't catch Disc-mounted units or trade efficiently into a 4+ invuln wall backed by heavy engine fire. It cracks open when massed Melta and concentrated AP-3+ focus fire — particularly from Chaos Knights Infernal Lance or T'au Mont'ka — strip the Daemon Engines turn one before the Enlightened can dictate engagement range.
489: Built around Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, a Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, and dense Tzaangor chaff, this is the Cult of Magic's classic layered-body list — slow, wide, and punishment-coded across every phase. The win condition is primary-score dominance through sheer OC weight: Rubrics sticky objectives via All is Dust durability (AP-1 shooting literally does nothing against them), Terminators anchor the midfield with a 2+/4++ that forces the opponent to commit AP-3+ firepower just to shift them, while Tzaangors and Enlightened screen and contest flanks the Terminators can't reach. It punishes static gunlines hard — Russ tanks and Devastator-equivalents waste shots on Rubrics that ignore their volume fire, and Terminators absorb the heavy anti-tank that was meant for vehicles. Fast melee toolboxes and mobile anti-armour are the nemesis: Infernal Lance Despoilers with AP-3+ Melta concentrate through the 4++ before the list can spread damage back, and deepstriking Skorpekh or Khornate elites bypass the Tzaangor screen to hit the Terminator brick before its psychic buffs have cycled.
427: Built around Commander Farsight leading a wall of Crisis suits — Coldstar, Enforcer, Sunforge, Fireknife, and Starscythe variants — this is the Mont'ka Battlesuit Spam list, six distinct Crisis chassis all doing different jobs at once. The engine is Jump-Shoot-Jump repositioning: every turn, Crisis suits close to Melta or Cyclic Ion Blaster range, spike a priority target with concentrated AP-3+ fire, then reposition out of counter-fire arcs before the opponent can respond. It punishes static gunlines and low-invuln vehicle parks mercilessly — the Coldstar's 40" threat range and Sunforge Melta output can delete a T9 chassis per turn cycle while Fireknife suits strip infantry screening from safety. Lists that can match its movement speed or force it into unfavorable engagement ranges crack it open: fast melee delivery (Berzerker Warband Rhino-rush, Custodes Talons closing across open ground) and anti-vehicle spam at range catches the JSJ window before it closes.
485: Built around the Norn Emissary, Maleceptor, and Tyrannofex anchoring a Synapse-dense monster roster, this is a Synaptic Nexus or Invasion Fleet castle — a T8-10 monster wall that layers Synapse bubbles across the midfield to lock down objectives. The engine is durable high-Toughness bodies absorbing the opponent's alpha strike while the Norn Assimilator and Screamer-Killers close range to engage on turn 2-3, with the Tyrannofex providing long-range AP-2 fire support to threaten vehicles without overcommitting melee. It punishes static gunlines and transport-mech lists that can't reposition out of melee threat range, because T9-10 chassis with FNP-equivalent Synapse buffs are simply too expensive to trade off efficiently with Russ Demolisher or Rhino-delivered hammers. Concentrated AP-3+ Melta and fast mobile anti-armour — Knights or Mont'ka Crisis suits at 12" range — crack it open, because the monster wall has no invulnerable save layer to fall back on when wound rolls land on 3+ to wound against T9.
484: Built around the Norn Assimilator as its centrepiece monster, backed by a visceral support crew of Pyrovores, Psychophage, Haruspex, and Tyrant Guard screening bodies — all delivered through Talons of the Norn Queen's monster-buffing framework wrapped inside the Assimilation Swarm's deepstrike-and-consume engine. The plan is to use Ripper Swarm chaff to clog midfield objectives while the Norn Assimilator and Haruspex crash into priority targets turn 2, farming the Assimilation Swarm's consumption triggers to snowball primary scoring and generate free reinforcements that compound each turn. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count vehicle lists that can't clear both the Ripper blob screen and a T10+ Norn Assimilator simultaneously — the activation gap forces impossible choices. It cracks open against fast AP-3+ anti-armour pressure and Lethal Hits volume shooting, both of which can strip the monster core before the consumption engine gets going and leave the Ripper screens stranded without their hammer to follow up.
496: Built around Bloodletters, Flesh Hounds, Bloodcrushers, and Skarbrand supported by a Lord on Juggernaut and a Forgefiend, this is a Goretrack Onslaught list running daemon-heavy cavalry and summoned infantry as its primary hammers. The engine is a layered threat stack: Bloodcrushers and Flesh Hounds close distance and absorb the alpha strike on their 4+ invuln, then Skarbrand and the Lord on Juggernaut deliver the killing blow into whatever the opponent just committed to clear the screen, with the Forgefiend punishing any exposed T7-9 vehicle that tries to stay out of the melee. Against mid-table brawlers and transport-infantry lists, the combination of Juggernaut mobility, Lethal Hits volume from the Khorne daemon weapon profiles, and layered 4+ invuln means most charge-back counters simply don't clear enough models to stop the next wave. It folds to heavy melta concentration and mass AP-3+ fire — Mont'ka Battlesuits or Infernal Lance Knights match its speed while cracking the daemon cavalry at range before Skarbrand can close, and once Skarbrand is gone the list loses its single dominant damage spike.
500: Built around Purestrain Genestealers and Neophyte Hybrid blobs backed by Achilles Ridgerunners, Atalan Jackals, and Reductus Saboteurs, this is Biosanctic Broodsurge running a wide-roster scoring machine with genuine teeth across every phase. The engine is body-count dominance — Neophyte blobs plant on objectives while Purestrains deepstrike or infiltrate into the opponent's scoring pieces, Ridgerunner indirect fire clears screens, and Saboteurs disrupt key units before the Acolyte Hand Flamer squads close in. At a balanced win rate it punishes static gunlines and transport-heavy lists that can't clear 30+ bodies per turn while also absorbing anti-infantry volume through sheer model count and distributed threat vectors. It struggles against fast kiting lists that deny the Purestrain charge window and concentrated Melta or blast-template fire that can clear Neophyte blobs before they lock objectives.
501: Built around Aberrants and Abominant anchored by Biophagus buffs, with Purestrain Genestealers and Hand Flamer Acolytes as the assault wave and Achilles Ridgerunners providing long-range anti-armour cover. The plan is to flood objectives with high-OC, high-wound bodies that are genuinely difficult to clear — Aberrants at T5 with a 4+ invuln via Biophagus's Alchemicus Symbiote stack force opponents into unfavorable trades while Purestrains and Acolytes pressure flanks and secondaries. This list punishes Heavy Gunline and Mid-T Brawler matchups by presenting too many durable bodies to efficiently remove before the GSC scores primary, with the Ridgerunners' mining laser coverage threatening any vehicle that tries to sit back and chip. It cracks open into fast skimmer lists and Mobile Anti-Armour threats — Knights and Mont'ka can spike the Aberrant blobs through AP-3+ before the Biophagus buffs pay off, and Drukhari kite cleanly outside Hand Flamer threat range where the list has no answer at speed.
518: Built around Lokhust Lords leading Lokhust Destroyers and Heavy Destroyers alongside Skorpekh Lords with Skorpekh Destroyers — the full Destroyer Cult stack buffed by Cursed Legion's +2 Strength chain trigger — this list runs a Technomancer keeping the damage dealers on the table via Reanimation while the kill-chain compounds across activations. The engine is the Cursed Legion buff cascade: destroy or halve an enemy unit with one Destroyer Cult piece and every other Necron in the army picks up +2 Strength that turn, turning mid-priority shooting and melee into threat-range spikes that clear objectives faster than the opponent can replace screening bodies. Heavy Destroyers' Gauss Destructor profiles at S14 AP-4 punish T7-9 vehicle lists and elite infantry bricks that rely on 2+/4++ saves, while Lethal Hits volume from the Lokhust suite sidesteps toughness thresholds entirely on key wound rolls. The list cracks open when static gunlines or massed Blast templates — Russ Demolishers, Plagueburst Crawlers — pop the Technomancer early and cut Reanimation support, leaving expensive Destroyer units stranded without the repair loop that makes their attrition math work.
503: Built around Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, and a Librarian in Terminator Armour as the melee hammer, with Caanok Var and an Ancient in Terminator Armour stacking aura buffs across the brick — this is a 1st Company Task Force-style deep-striking Terminator wall with genuine multi-axis firepower. The engine is a Turn 2 deepstrike commit: the entire Terminator mass drops into mid-board, uses Librarian psychic buffs and the Ancient's re-roll aura to spike damage, and then grinds primary through sheer wound pool and OC while Lethal Hits procs from stacked abilities punish anything that tries to clear them. It punishes Transport Infantry and Mid-T Brawler lists hard — the 2+/5++ Terminator chassis absorbs Rhino-disembark counter-punches and Ork mob charges without flinching, and volume-fire from 2-wound T5 models clears Cultist screens efficiently. It cracks open against Mobile Anti-Armour: concentrated AP-3+ Melta at 12" range from Mont'ka Battlesuits or Knight Despoilers can erase an entire Terminator unit before the Librarian's defensive strats fire, and the build's zero-kite profile means it eats every Melta shot it faces.
517: Built around Doomsday Arks as the long-range backbone, Silent King as the anchor, and Lychguard plus Flayed Ones providing close-quarters threat, this is Starshatter Arsenal operating as a hybrid gunline-control list. The plan is to plant Doomsday Arks in second-row firing positions — the Doomsday Cannon's S16 AP-5 D6+6 profile deletes T9-12 chassis reliably from 60" — while Tomb Blades screen midfield and Lychguard with Dispersion Shields absorb the counter-punch under the Silent King's reanimation and Obeisance aura. It punishes slow durable-grind and Heavy Gunline opponents through superior threat range and the layered Reanimation Protocols plus 4+ invuln on Lychguard, which forces inefficient trade-targeting on lists that can't close distance fast. Fast mobile lists with AP-3+ melta — Mont'ka Battlesuits or Infernal Lance Knights — crack it open by closing the 24" min-range dead zone on the Doomsday Cannon before the Ark can reposition, stripping its hull integrity in a single activation spike.
505: Built around Redemptor and Brutalis Dreadnoughts supported by Techmarines keeping them fighting-fit, this is an Ironstorm Spearhead or Anvil Siege Force expression that treats T8 walkers as both the gunline and the hammer. The plan is to anchor Redemptors in mid-board firing lanes with Hellblasters amplifying the plasma spike, then crash Brutalis chassis into anything that survives — Techmarines providing Blessing of the Omnissiah repairs each turn to recycle hull points the opponent spent resources removing. It punishes static shooting armies and low-model-count vehicle lists that can't concentrate enough AP-2+ fire to remove a repaired T8 chassis before it deletes their own platforms. What cracks it open is volume: horde infantry or activation-rich mech lists contest the objectives its slow walkers can't reach, and anti-tank focus fire that outpaces the Techmarine repair economy will eventually strand the Brutalis short of its charge.
504: Built around Land Speeders and Storm Speeder Hammerstrike/Thunderstrike platforms backed by Vindicators, this is an Ironstorm Spearhead-style mobile fire-base that combines fast-skimmer anti-armour with heavy demolisher blast support. The engine is closing Hammerstrikes to Melta range (Str 9 AP-3 Melta D6+2) while Thunderstrikes lock down vehicles with Str 10 assault rockets, and Vindicator Demolisher Cannons punish anything that clusters; Incursors and Outriders screen the chassis and contest objectives to keep primary scoring on track. It punishes slow armoured gunlines and T7-9 vehicle lists hard — the Hammerstrike's Melta paired with the Vindicator's S14 AP-3 creates an anti-armour overload that even Knight-equivalent saves can't absorb across two activation windows. The weakness is high-activation horde lists and melee delivery armies — 30-Boyz mobs or Possessed-in-Land-Raiders can tar-pit the low-model-count chassis, and once Speeders are locked in combat they can't fire-and-fade.
515: Built around paired Exocrines and Tyrannofexes as fire-base anchors, screened by Termagant and Hormagaunt blobs with Gargoyles providing fast mid-board coverage and a Maleceptor stacking Synaptic pressure — this is a Crusher Stampede or Invasion Fleet shell pushing a static shooting identity rare for the faction. The plan is to plant the Exocrines and Tyrannofexes in optimal fire lanes while the gaunt swarms bury objectives under raw OC, letting the heavy guns delete threats piecemeal rather than committing the monsters to melee trades. The Termagant and Hormagaunt volume (high wound pools, cheap OC) punishes low-activation gunlines that can't clear blobs efficiently before the Exocrines delete their key fire platforms — a strong angle into Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists that expect to outscore on primary against fragile screens. However, the list folds to Mobile Anti-Armour pressure: a Mont'ka or Infernal Lance player can match its threat range, concentrate AP-3+ Melta onto the T8 Exocrine and Tyrannofex chassis before the screen closes the distance, and the list has no real answer once its shooting base is dismantled.
531: Built around Custodian Guard as the scoring anvil, Venatari Custodians and Vertus Praetors as fast flanking hammers, and Contemptor-Achillus Dreadnoughts as elite line-breakers, this is a Shield Host list that plays like a transport-infantry rush wearing terminator armor — mass 2+/4++ bodies delivered aggressively across the midboard. The engine is activation-count pressure: multiple distinct elite units converge on objectives simultaneously, forcing the opponent to split anti-elite resources while Custodian Guard sticky-claims behind them. It punishes low-model-count anti-armour and gunline lists that can't clear 2+/4++ models efficiently before the scoring clock runs out — each Russ or Knight shot that fails to break through a five-man Custodian Guard blob is a primary point conceded. The weakness is anything that floods the board with bodies or delivers concentrated AP-3 Melta, since the list's low activation count loses the primary race against true hordes and T9-chassis Melta fire drops Allarus and Dreadnoughts before the 4++ math can bail them out.
530: Built around Vertus Praetors, Allarus Custodians, a Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike, and Witchseekers riding in Land Raiders, Lions of the Emperor delivers elite infantry via transport, blending Custodes melee brutality with Sisters of Silence psychic denial into a single cohesive battleline. The engine is transport-rush scoring: Land Raiders push Custodian Guard and Allarus bricks onto midfield objectives while Vertus Praetors and the Dawneagle Shield-Captain threaten flanks, and Witchseekers in the same delivery shell deny Psychic actions and Warp-adjacency buffs the opponent relies on. The 2+/4++ profile across virtually every model means volume-fire lists — Mass Volume Horde infantry blobs, Mid-T Brawler mobs — cannot trade efficiently into the brick, and the Caladius Grav-Tank provides the AP-2 ranged spine to punish anything that tries to screen the advance. It cracks under concentrated AP-3+ Melta pressure at range — Mobile Anti-Armour lists like Infernal Lance or Mont'ka Crisis Battlesuits can strip hull points from the Land Raiders before the cargo deploys, stranding the expensive melee pieces in the open.
525: Built around Land Speeder Vengances, Invader ATVs, Outrider Squads, Ravenwing Black Knights, and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Company of Hunters is a fast all-vehicle Ravenwing list that brings anti-armour firepower and objective harassment from a fully mechanised, hover-capable roster. The engine is mid-range volume fire on the move — Plasma Talon and Assault Cannon fire from advancing Speeders and ATVs strips MEQ units off objectives while Black Knights threaten melee follow-through on isolated targets, converting tempo into primary scoring before the opponent stabilises. The list punishes slow defensive shells that can't dictate engagement range: static gunlines and transport infantry built around Rhino delivery get outflanked and eroded by units that fire at full effect while advancing, and the high activation count exploits the gap against 3-5 vehicle lists contesting fewer objectives. It folds to concentrated anti-armour overload — AP-3+ Melta from Knights or Mont'ka Battlesuits tracks and removes the fragile T5-6 skimmer chassis faster than the list can reposition, and without an infantry scoring base the primary race becomes unwinnable once the vehicles start dying.
532: Built around Custodian Guard delivered alongside Allarus Custodians, Witchseekers, Vertus Praetors, and Caladius Grav-Tanks, this is the Talons of the Emperor transport-infantry expression — a gold-clad Rhino-rush analogue where elite bodies push forward in mixed-unit waves rather than a single deathball. The plan is to use Vertus Praetors as the advance screen, land Allarus Custodians via teleport-strike onto priority targets, and grind primary with Custodian Guard blobs whose 2+/4++ makes them nearly impossible to shift off objectives in a single activation. It punishes Mid-T Brawler lists hardest — where War Horde and Da Big Hunt rely on volume attacks to out-trade elite units, the 2+/4++ stack across every model means even 30 Boyz throwing 60 attacks fail to clear a Custodian Guard squad, and the Caladius provides the AP-3+ anti-vehicle coverage to pop transports before the counter-charge arrives. The list cracks under concentrated Mobile Anti-Armour fire — Knights or Mont'ka Melta at AP-3+ focused into the Caladius turn one collapses the anti-armour backbone, leaving the foot units exposed on primary with no answer to T9+ chassis.
527: Built around Lokhust Destroyers supported by the Lokhust Lord and Nekrosor Ammentar, with Ophydian Destroyers and Canoptek Wraiths as the melee enforcement layer and a Canoptek Reanimator keeping the whole engine alive, this is the Awakened Dynasty's Destroyer Cult expression — a fast, self-healing mid-board threat rather than the classic C'tan castle. The win condition is teleporting or advancing the Destroyer stack into firing range while Ophydians surface behind screens to peel support characters, letting the Lokhust volley delete isolated units before Reanimator protocols restore lost models and repeat the cycle. The 4+ invuln on Wraiths and the layered FNP-equivalent from Reanimator protocols punish static gunlines that can't clear Necron units in a single activation window. The engine collapses if the Lokhust Lord or Ammentar dies early — losing the wound-reroll and buff stacking cuts Lokhust damage output significantly, and a Mobile Anti-Armour list with concentrated AP-3+ Melta can strip the key characters before the Reanimator stabilizes the squad.
522: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard bricks, Cthonian Beserks, and Hekaton Land Fortresses backed by Hernkyn Pioneer screening and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn fire support, this is the Hearthband's signature combined-arms hammer — T5-6 melee elites delivered forward on a chassis of fast scouts and a T10 battle tank. The engine is a War Horde-adjacent brawl: Beserks and Hearthguard close under Pioneer and Sagitaur screening, contest mid-board with high OC and punishing Sustained Hits 1-equivalent melee output, while Hekaton Land Fortresses and Thunderkyn delete the vehicles and elite infantry that threaten the advance. It punishes low-model-count anti-armour lists — Knights and Mont'ka shooters — because the activation gap is brutal when you're fielding 12+ units of T5-6 bodies that soak AP-3 and keep contesting objectives. What cracks it open is concentrated blast-template fire from Heavy Gunline builds: Russ Demolisher companies and Anvil Siege Force heavy-weapon stations can strip Beserks and Hearthguard faster than the Votann trading engine recoups the losses, leaving the Hekaton exposed on a primary race it can't win alone.
523: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Cthonian Beserks, and Hernkyn Pioneers backed by a Hekaton Land Fortress, this is the Hearthband index detachment playing a brutally straightforward mid-board brawl. The list floods objectives with T5 bodies — Hearthguard bricks and Beserks threatening melee — while Brôkhyr Thunderkyn and the Land Fortress provide the fire support that forces opponents to either engage the melee threat or die to the gunline. It punishes low-activation vehicle lists like Infernal Lance and Questoris builds hard, where the sheer activation count and sustained T5 wound pools on multiple squads overwhelm a 3-5 chassis roster's ability to clear objectives before the scoring gap becomes unrecoverable. Against fast kiting lists — Reaper's Wager Drukhari or Aspect Host — the lack of meaningful movement tricks leaves Hearthguard bricks unable to catch skimmers, and the Votann's middling invulnerable saves mean sustained Lethal Hits fire from Dark Reapers or sustained Splinter volume chips away at what looks durable but isn't.
529: Built around Wolf Guard Headtakers and Terminators led by Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Logan Grimnar, and a Wolf Priest, Saga of the Beastslayer delivers an elite, character-stacked melee hammer backed by the battlefield's most durable ancients. The engine is forcing close-range engagements where Headtakers and Terminators drop out of transports or stride forward behind Bjorn's Venerable Dreadnought chassis, leveraging Wolf Priest reroll auras and Logan's Command buff to spike damage on priority targets while contesting midfield objectives through sheer model durability. The build punishes low-activation gunlines and fragile skimmer lists alike — Wolf Guard Terminators with 2+/5++ shrug off Splinter Pistol and S5 chip fire while Headtaker melee output overwhelms anything that can't clear T5 at volume. However, mass-blast templates and dedicated anti-infantry horde removal (Russ Demolishers, Punisher Cannons, or mob-tarpitting Boyz flooding objectives) expose the low model count, leaving the list unable to contest the primary scoring race once its expensive hammers are tied down or deleted piecemeal.
528: Built around Logan Grimnar leading Wolf Guard Terminators and Wolf Guard Headtakers, with Bjorn the Fell-Handed as a durable anchor and Grey Hunters filling out the battleline, this is a Champions of Russ mixed-elite force that leans on character-stacking and transport delivery to get its hammers into contact. The engine is Logan's command aura amplifying Wolf Guard crit-fishing — Headtakers in particular want to be in melee where their extra attacks on unmodified hit rolls of 6 generate the kill chain — while Grey Hunters in Rhinos claim objectives and Bjorn's T9 chassis absorbs the anti-tank budget that would otherwise target the elite infantry. It punishes mid-range brawlers and transport-infantry lists that can't clear a 2+/4++ Terminator brick before Logan's aura starts compounding, and Bjorn's Dreadnought durability forces opponents to commit dedicated anti-armour to a non-scoring unit. It cracks open against concentrated AP-3+ shooting and fast skimmer kiting — the list's glacial movement means Wave Serpents and Raiders can dictate range indefinitely, and without reliable long-range anti-tank the Rhino delivery plan collapses if transports get popped turn one.
521: Built around Stealth Battlesuits and Ghostkeels as forward-deployed threat-denial pieces, backed by a Riptide and Broadsides providing heavy firepower, this is a Mont'ka-style list that uses permanent Stealth and Shroudshroud stacking to project pressure where static gunlines can't answer. The engine is Pathfinder-fed markerlight chains unlocking full BS2+ on the Riptide's Heavy Burst Cannon and Broadside missile racks while Piranhas and Stealth suits use their high movement to contest midfield objectives and force the opponent off scoring positions before they can stabilize. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Mass Volume Horde matchups hard — the Riptide's Blast-profile Heavy Burst Cannon clears infantry blobs efficiently at S6 volume, while the Broadsides' AP-2 missile saturation makes static tank companies pay for standing still. Mobile anti-armour lists like Infernal Lance or Imperial Knights match the T'au movement budget and carry the Melta and AP-3+ firepower to strip the T6-7 battlesuit chassis before the markerlight chain comes online, which is where this list comes apart.
520: Built around Riptide Battlesuits, Stealth Battlesuits, and Ghostkeels running a Mont'ka-flavored mobile-fire framework, this list uses Pathfinders and Sky Ray Gunships to light up priority targets while fast harassment pieces — Piranhas and Stealth suits — deny deepstrike corridors and hold secondary objectives. The engine is target-priority via sensor lock: Pathfinder Markerlight chains strip cover and impose BS penalties, letting Riptide Nova Charge shots and Sky Ray Seeker Missiles hit T7-9 chassis at AP-3+ efficiency while Piranhas contest Engage on All Fronts and Behind Enemy Lines secondaries the opponent can't answer. It punishes heavy gunline and static anti-armour lists hard — neither a Russ company nor a Knight brick can dictate range against Jump-Shoot-Jump Riptides and 8"-move skimmer harassment that scores secondaries in their backfield. Where it cracks is against volume-infantry horde lists that flood objectives with raw OC faster than the low-model-count T'au roster can contest, and against aggressive melee delivery lists that close before the sensor-lock chain is established.
